correctness.rationale: From the exact ellipse arclength parametrization the diagonal Hessian entries are p times the integral of (R^2)^(p/2-1)(1+(p-2)X_i^2/R^2)w(t). Reflection symmetry removes mixed terms; analyticity holds for p,epsilon near zero. At epsilon=0 the normalized Hessian G_i=H_ii/(pi p) equals p exactly, while d_epsilon G_2(p,0)=-(p-1)(p-2)/2, giving derivatives (d_p,d_epsilon)=(1,-1) at zero. The p=0 logarithmic potential is harmonic near the ellipse center; semiaxis interchange makes G_2(0,epsilon) odd, so d_epsilon^2 G_2(0,0)=0. The analytic implicit function theorem then yields epsilon_*=p+3p^2/2+O(p^3); positivity of G_1 and strict decrease of G_2 yield minimum versus saddle. Independent adaptive quadrature found epsilon_*(0.04)=0.0427457988944, epsilon_*(0.02)=0.0206398375595 and epsilon_*(0.01)=0.0101547949188, consistent with the stated coefficient and higher-order remainder.
residual_risks: The zero-Hessian critical curve is not a proven strict extremum and no such claim is made.
